title: Meteorology and Atmospheric Science, B.S. (College of Earth and Mineral Sciences)
notes:
Built from the archived 2024-2025 bulletin (https://bulletins.psu.edu/archive/2024-2025/undergraduate/colleges/earth-mineral-sciences/meteorology-atmospheric-science-bs/). This program's Atmospheric Science option and Common Requirements are byte-identical across the 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 archived bulletins (verified by diffing all three years' extracted Program Requirements and Suggested Academic Plan tables against each other directly) -- this file's notes apply equally to METEO-2023.json and METEO-2024.json. All 8 semesters of the Suggested Academic Plan (course codes, per-semester credits, and the page's own stated 121-credit total) match METEO-2026.json's course sequence exactly. Two real, verified differences from the 2025-26/2026-27 curriculum, both confirmed against the archived program-requirements text and the archived METEO course-description page:
1) The Atmospheric Science Option's Professional-Elective-eligible course pool ended in 'METEO 480W' (Undergraduate Research) rather than 2025-26's 'METEO 481' (Weather Communications I) -- both are real, separately-existing courses (confirmed on the archived department course-description page), so the Professional Elective 'match' regex here swaps 480W back in for 481. (The list's other 'METEO 471' citation, without a 'W' suffix, is kept as METEO 471W -- the department page confirms no separate plain 'METEO 471' course exists, only 'METEO 471W: Atmospheric Optics', so this is the bulletin's own inconsistent citation, not a real code difference.)
2) The Common Requirements table's STAT credit was a 3cr 'Select one of the following: EBF 472, STAT 301, STAT 401' choice rather than 2025-26's fixed STAT 401 Prescribed Course. Kept STAT 401 modeled here (unchanged from METEO-2026.json) since it was, and remains, a fully valid pick among the three, and is the only one with a verified normal University Park prereq chain in this codebase's own catalog data (STAT 301 is flagged there as a Behrend-only course number not published in the university-wide undergraduate bulletin; EBF 472 isn't in this codebase's EBF catalog at all) -- recording the real broader historical choice here rather than adding unverifiable extra options.
Also re-verified CHEM 110's real prerequisite ('Completion of or placement beyond MATH 22') and MATH 22/21/4/3's own chain directly against this year's archived university-wide course-description pages (2024-2025) -- unchanged from 2026, so the same MATH 3/4/21/22 explicit-add fix (Semesters 1-4) and the same max_credits_per_semester=18 (133cr total vs. 128cr capacity at the original 16cr/semester cap) apply for the same reasons documented in METEO-2026.json. Minor, non-modeled bulletin-text differences also present this year but not reflected in the plan (consistent with METEO-2026.json's own existing conventions of not tracking every textual variant): the Communication/Writing pick was printed as plain 'CAS 100 or ENGL 202C' (2 options, no 'ENGL/CAS 138T') rather than 2025-26's 3-option 'CAS 100A, ENGL/CAS 138T, or ENGL 202C' -- 'CAS 100' is the same registrar course as CAS 100A (the modern catalog only recognizes the lettered CAS 100A/B/C/S sections), and ENGL 138T already existed as a real course in this year's own university-wide bulletin even though this program page didn't separately enumerate it, so the Communication item is kept unchanged from METEO-2026.json; the Electives credit range printed as '4-9' rather than 2025-26's '5-10' (bookkeeping-only, doesn't change any specific course); and the programming-course pick listed 'METEO 273, CMPSC 101, CMPSC 200, CMPSC 201, or CMPSC 202' (5 options, including a since-dropped CMPSC 202) vs. 2025-26's 4 options -- unchanged since this plan already only ever modeled the fixed METEO 273 pick, not the full alternative list, in any year.
